title: Ecological niche and phylogeography elucidate complex biogeographic patterns in Loxosceles rufescens (Araneae, Sicariidae) in the Mediterranean Basin
problem: Understanding the evolutionary history of the cryptic spider *Loxosceles rufescens* is challenging because long-term, human-mediated dispersal throughout the Mediterranean has obscured natural biogeographic patterns, creating a mismatch between genetic relationships and geographic location.
method: This paper integrates phylogeographic analyses of mitochondrial DNA with ecological niche modeling to elucidate the complex evolutionary history and biogeographic patterns of the spider *Loxosceles rufescens* in the Mediterranean Basin, a history complicated by cryptic lineages and human-mediated dispersal.
task: The task is to elucidate the complex evolutionary history and biogeographic patterns of the spider *Loxosceles rufescens* in the Mediterranean Basin by integrating ecological niche models with phylogeographic analyses to understand its origins and the impact of human-mediated dispersal.
innovation: By integrating ecological niche models with phylogeographic analyses, this study elucidates the complex evolutionary history of the spider *Loxosceles rufescens*, revealing a North African origin, Pleistocene diversification in multiple refugia, and a current distribution significantly shaped by human-mediated dispersal.
